rules.text: When a pull request names or changes a plan, verify the implementation against that plan's stated phase deliverables, acceptance evidence, tests, and cross-stack symbols; changing expected files alone is not evidence of completion.

Every new struct, function, component, event, payload, registry entry, schema, asset ID, or configuration field must have a reachable production producer, consumer, registration, and loading path as applicable; reject disconnected definitions and tests that only inject the missing connection manually.

Preserve Bong's server Rust, agent TypeScript, and client Fabric boundaries. Cross-layer changes must update every affected producer, wire schema, generated or mirrored representation, converter, consumer, and contract test.

TypeBox schemas are the IPC source of truth. Schema or enum changes must update generated JSON Schema, Rust serde mirrors, shared samples, and all consumers; agent code that imports @bong/schema must also receive the rebuilt distribution artifact when required.

For server_data and other protobuf-to-JSON bridges, verify the real wire representation end to end: protobuf enums, uint64 string encoding, flattened coordinates, Rust conversion, emission, JsonFormat conversion, and client field access must agree exactly.

SPIRIT_QI_TOTAL conservation is mandatory. Every qi or spirit-qi movement must be represented by qi_physics ledger transfer semantics with a real state-applying consumer; direct one-sided increments, decrements, dropped off-screen snapshots, or audit-only transfer events that do not update WorldQiAccount are merge blockers.

Do not invent local qi decay, drain, attenuation, half-life, density, or similar physical constants or formulas. Reuse qi_physics constants and helpers, or extend qi_physics first and import the canonical definition.

The only permitted system outflow is the tracked Tiandao era decay path. It must move qi into era_decay_accum so current_total plus era_decay_accum remains equal to initial_total; it must not silently evaporate qi.
The six canonical realms, in order, are 醒灵, 引气, 凝脉, 固元, 通灵, 化虚. Reject legacy cultivation names such as 练气, 筑基, 金丹, or 元婴 in new gameplay and user-facing content.
骨币 is the only true currency. Minerals are barter goods, 灵石 is a degraded fuel rather than currency, and gold or silver is not a canonical money system.
New names must fit the depleted末法 setting. Avoid 玄, 陨, 星, 仙, 太, 古 except established mundane mineral names, and prefer plain decayed imagery such as 残, 碎, 锈, 杂, 粗, 髓, 朴, 枯.

New or changed zones must agree with existing canonical zone IDs and their worldgen/server consumers. Reject duplicate concepts, renamed IDs without migrations, or a blueprint/raster/runtime mismatch.

Worldgen terrain fields must remain registered through LAYER_REGISTRY, including safe_default, blend_mode, and export_type. Stitching, raster export, and Rust runtime interpretation must derive from the same layer contract.

Worldgen raster exports and Rust readers must agree on layer order, dimensions, little-endian element type, safe defaults, and mmap layout; regenerated manifests and postconditions must accompany contract changes.

Keep Bevy ECS data and behavior separated: components represent state, systems perform logic, queries exclude terminal markers where required, and client-visible Valence entities must use Despawned rather than bare despawn before the entity layer update pass.

Do not use armor stands, invisible mobs, or other vanilla entities as custom collision or interaction carriers. Bong custom entities use Marker plus custom rendering, with interaction sent through an explicit client-to-server intent request.

The server must tolerate vanilla or bot clients that omit, delay, or send malformed optional Fabric payloads without panic or disconnect unless the protocol contract explicitly requires rejection. New gameplay modules need an appropriate headless bot scenario when an end-to-end client/server path exists.

Every implemented active skill or cast must ship a distinct animation, particle or VFX, SFX, HUD feedback, and SkillBar or hotbar PNG icon through real server-schema-client wiring. A server-only operator, enum-only stub, shared generic feedback, or unregistered icon is incomplete.

Locked, inactive, or unavailable abilities and styles must not remain permanently visible as disabled HUD clutter; conditional HUD elements should be hidden until their authoritative state makes them relevant.

PlayerAnimator loops need endTick keys for every animated axis, large leg motion must avoid unsupported IK poses, torso-only motion must not misuse body transforms, and bend-dependent animation requires the existing bendy-lib integration.

Any committed client asset change that affects the distributed resource pack must update the server resource-pack SHA-1 and committed manifest size/hash bindings so runtime delivery and CI remain synchronized.

ItemCategory must use only its canonical enum variants. In particular, alchemy or crafting materials use Misc rather than a nonexistent Material category; one invalid registry entry can invalidate the entire item registry.

Tests must lock every observable contract changed or claimed by the pull request across its happy paths, boundaries including empty, maximum, and off-by-one cases, invalid inputs and every error branch, permission and state preconditions, every enum variant, and every state transition including self or no-op transitions where the contract permits them. Schema, enum, and state-machine changes require dedicated positive and negative pin tests. Cross-stack producer-to-wire-to-consumer contracts require an integration test when unit tests cannot expose the full break. Missing one of these required contract categories is a major defect when it leaves changed behavior unprotected or permits a concrete incorrect implementation to pass; documentation or pull requests that falsely claim nonexistent coverage are also defects. Finer assertions or extra cases around behavior already fully protected by this contract are suggestions.

Do not classify newly appearing failures as pre-existing without proof. A batch of failures sharing registry, asset, schema, or initialization signatures should be traced to the common change, and piped build commands must preserve the actual producer exit status.

Prefer the smallest complete and maintainable implementation. Compatibility layers without an explicit migration need, speculative abstractions without a present requirement, inconsistent duplicate sources of truth, and broad refactors unrelated to the requested outcome are major defects because they expand the supported surface and obscure the authoritative path even before a production failure is observed. Also treat demonstrated production failures, unreachable production wiring, non-atomic state, unbounded resource paths, and structures that materially prevent a required correct change as major defects.

For pull requests whose changes are limited to docs/ plan documents (plan-* and plans-skeleton design-closure PRs), limit review scope to internal consistency, factual accuracy of code citations, alignment with plan-refactor-master-v1 scope and cross-track dependencies, and satisfaction of the acceptance criteria stated in the PR description or the document itself. Depth expansions beyond those criteria - new scenarios, extra edge-case enumerations, additional contract surfaces - are suggestions for the open-questions section, not major or blocker findings; an explicit open-questions entry with rationale is a valid resolution for a deferred design decision.

Classify comments that merely restate obvious code, clearer naming, optional helper extraction or reuse, simplification of already-correct branches, finer assertions around behavior already fully protected by the saturated-tests contract, and extra defensive checks without a reachable failure as suggestions; these bounded improvements do not gate the review. This rule does not downgrade speculative abstractions, compatibility layers without migration need, duplicate sources of truth, unrelated scope growth, or missing required contract tests.
